verification_report.summary: The supplied supplement is correct under the stated hypotheses and accepted prerequisites. Every proof item was checked in textual order. The obstacle lemma correctly combines normalized L1 control with negative weighted sums: the partial sums have uniformly bounded L1 norms and curvature bounded below by -A omega, so their limit is genuine; its pole set and the countable obstacle exceptions would make K locally pluripolar, giving the required contradiction. For the envelope, q+min_K w is admissible. For every competitor a, b=max(a-C,q) is a normalized Q competitor because its Lelong numbers on every local modification equal those of varphi. Thus q+min_K w<=E<=q+C, yielding ordinary singularity equivalence with q and multiplier-ideal equivalence with varphi at every positive weight. Choquet selection, admissible finite maxima and countably many locally pluripolar exceptions preserve the obstacle after regularization. Hence E is an actual largest competitor and the original pointwise supremum equals E everywhere. The local regularization exception theorem is also corroborated by [Demailly, Corollary 8.9](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/nice_cimpa.pdf). Class dependence, both monotonicities, translation, the two Lipschitz inequalities at poles, joint concavity and the exact smooth gauge identity all follow with the stated signs and quantifiers. Connectedness supplies the normalized compactness hypothesis; compact K and continuous real w supply finite extrema and norms. No global Josefson property, closedness of theta, positive or finite Monge-Ampere mass, BMP, or quotient-theorem input is used. The final quotient-theorem sentence is explanatory context and is not independently certified here. No contact-support, mass, or asymptotic conclusion is inferred.
